subject: Operational SLA exception and shared-responsibility playbook for AeroNova private VPC
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aeronova.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: maria.ruiz@aeronova.com, procure@procureit.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA apportionment & monitoring playbook for AeroNova private VPC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the onboarding call yesterday. As discussed, AeroNova will host Redwood’s inference runtime inside our VPC and operate the underlying network and edge routers. To move forward with procurement we need an explicit operational playbook that spells out:

- What Redwood will guarantee (service-layer availability, per-region failover) vs. what AeroNova must operate (border routers, private peering, transit)
- How latency SLOs are apportioned when the customer network is implicated (e.g., transit tail, peering flaps)
- Monitoring and alerting responsibilities (who raises severity-1 vs. advisory) and required evidence for audits

I’ve attached our network diagram and the security questionnaire for your review. Procurement needs a draft amendment and a DocuSign-ready template by next Friday (2027-08-20) to stay on the quarter close.

Attachments: aeronova_network_diagram.pdf (diagram), aeronova_security_questionnaire.xlsx (security answers)

Can Redwood provide a one-page SLA exception playbook + a proposed contract amendment that maps obligations to operational runbooks?

Best,
Samir
Director, Cloud Ops
AeroNova Systems

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aeronova.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA apportionment & monitoring playbook for AeroNova private VPC

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. We can produce a short operational playbook and a contract amendment that enumerates shared responsibilities. Quick summary of our approach:

1) Service commitments we can sign to: application-layer availability for model inference endpoints (uptime measured at Redwood ingress), KV-cache durability, and failover behavior for region-level outages.
2) Allocations: we'll propose a matrix that separates network ownership (customer-managed up to the VPC egress) from inference runtime SLOs. For latency we plan to:
   - commit p50/p95 token latency at the Redwood edge/router when traffic is healthy
   - exclude end-to-end latency SLOs from the commitment where customer-managed transit/peering is responsible; instead we will provide a guidance band and joint monitoring thresholds.
3) Monitoring & evidence: AeroNova must provide BGP/peering incident reports and flow logs for incidents claimed to be network-caused. Redwood will provide service telemetry, traces, and per-request metadata for auditing.

I’m looping in Vivek (runtime/infrastructure) and Neha (legal/sales) to draft the matrix and amendment. I’ll attach an initial SLA exception matrix CSV with the columns we usually use.

Attachment: redwood_sla_exception_matrix_v1.csv (draft)

Proposed next steps: internal technical review this week, contract language draft by 2027-08-13, DocuSign-ready amendment by 2027-08-18. Let me know if those dates work.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, samir.patel@aeronova.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA apportionment & monitoring playbook for AeroNova private VPC

Samir / team — quick technical clarifications from runtime side so the matrix is actionable:

- What Redwood can commit to:
  * Inference endpoint availability measured at our HTTP ingress (we can publish uptime in 5-minute buckets).
  * Model-serving latency measured inside the Redwood runtime (p50/p95/p99) assuming requests reach our ingress within normal network parameters.
  * KV-cache hit metrics and warm-start guarantees for pinned models.

- What we cannot realistically guarantee under private VPC:
  * End-to-end latency SLOs beyond our ingress (we can provide guidance but not guarantees for p99 tail) because customer networking and peering are variable and outside our control.
  * Network-level packet loss or transit jitter — these must be addressed via your NOC/peering teams.

- Proposed apportionment rule (operational):
  1) If Redwood telemetry indicates request processing failures (error rates above threshold) -> Redwood incident, Redwood remediation.
  2) If customer network reports loss/peering flap and packet-level evidence correlates with in-flight requests -> classify as Customer-Managed Network event; Redwood will provide request-level logs and ingestion timestamps for joint RCA.
  3) For borderline incidents (e.g., slow responses where both network and runtime show degradation) -> joint incident with timeboxed blame window and shared post-incident report.

Monitoring & evidence we will require from AeroNova for customer-managed incidents:
- Flow logs (sFlow/NetFlow), BGP update logs, and timestamps (UTC) for peering changes.
- Confirmation of any recent NAT/translation changes or border router config changes that align with incident windows.

I'll embed these rules into the SLA matrix CSV and add a small appendix describing the telemetry fields we will request for audits. Note: we will still support a runbook-level SLO labeling (e.g., "Runtime: 99.5% availability, excluding Customer Network Events") rather than a blanket uptime number that includes customer infra.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: samir.patel@aeronova.com
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA apportionment & monitoring playbook for AeroNova private VPC

Folks — from a contractual and procurement perspective I recommend two items be explicit in the amendment:

1) Shared-responsibility Table: a simple appendix that maps each SLO to the owning party, expected evidence, and the remediation credit rules when an SLO is missed and the cause is within Redwood's control.
2) Audit & Data Requests: timeline for evidence (e.g., customer provides network logs within 72 hours of request), permitted redaction rules, and an agreed cadence for joint post-incident reports.

I’ve updated the draft language in the amendment template to include:
- A definition for "Customer-Managed Network Event" with examples.
- A clause limiting Redwood’s latency guarantees to "inference runtime processing time at Redwood ingress" and excluding upstream/downstream transit.
- A procurement-friendly DocuSign instruction page so AeroNova can approve operational clauses without delaying the master services agreement.

I attached the revised amendment PDF (DocuSign-ready) and the HubSpot deal link for reference. Please confirm if procurement needs any additional sign-off rows (e.g., security ops acceptance).

Attachments: redwood_amendment_docusign.pdf
Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/78934

Neha Kapoor
Contracts & Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aeronova.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: maria.ruiz@aeronova.com, procure@procureit.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA apportionment & monitoring playbook for AeroNova private VPC

Priyom / Neha / Vivek — thanks for the quick turnaround and level-setting. AeroNova accepts the operational playbook approach and the shared-responsibility table as proposed. A couple of final asks before we route for signature:

- Please ensure the amendment includes an example incident timeline (how a joint RCA will be initiated and a 10-business-day target for the final report).
- Add a short clause that allows AeroNova to request temporary escalation credits (one-time, capped) if a regional peering issue causes production impact while both parties investigate.

If you can incorporate those two bullets and send the DocuSign package, procurement will start signature routing today. We expect the signed amendment by 2027-08-19.

Thanks — Samir
Director, Cloud Ops
AeroNova Systems
